title: Confusion and Vices of the Court
editorial_note: The translation keeps the court as a packed satirical crowd of bought rank, vice, and informers.

title: Roguish Life
text:
Roguish Life


I was placed in a poor cradle,

badly swaddled in coarse baize,

from which I came out robust and well

        tempered,

and my rustic hide much toughened.

To nature I have

        owed

more than the lord, the rich man, and the magnate,

for she made him restlessly

        delicate,

and me, with ease, well sturdy.

He covers himself in silk, which

        does not warm;

I resist inclemency with wool;

he is frightened by eating and

        grows fatigued,

while I am happy if I flatter my conscience,

for at every

        hour I fill my belly,

trusting that there is God and providence.
editorial_note: The source catalog title differs, but the body is 'Vida bribona'; this translation preserves its broken spacing.

title: Now Alone in My Heart
text:
Now alone in my heart

I have remained desertly;

the soul is like snow

spread out over the field,

the earth disappears,

the sky denies space,

the things that surround me

reject the light of habit.


What use are eyes to me?

What use the scent without a trace?

What use the voice without the name

that strips itself from the lip?

The time of my hope

is like time already past.

Now alone in my heart

I have remained desertly.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the repeated solitude and the unusual adverbial barrenness of 'desiertamente.'

title: Like a Warm Lily Advanced...
text:
Like a warm lily advanced

chastely between dawn and dew;

praying snow, dome of cold,

pure ogive, braided lightness.


Like a branch of the soul, revealed

neatly to unadorned light,

like the faith of sighing vigor

in a flight of tranquil flesh.


Like a dream of love directed,

in dawn of twin fountains,

toward the ecstasy of sheltered heaven.


Like a paired bird, risen without tremors,

calming in a wedded mystery

the human unease of flowers.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Ridruejo's sequence of chastely architectural and floral images.

title: Like an Adventurous Offering of Wheat...
text:
Like an adventurous offering of wheat

to give its passion to the sea,

you advanced, slender and morning-bright,

dressed and crowned in gentle gold.


Noon of the sun, prostrate earth

with mist of stupor, saline siesta;

and August in you, with the divine ripeness

of a solar tower, free and calm.


Fresh sword, the air of your passing

calmed the aridity while it burned,

holding up the heavens, miraculous.


Only my heart was sunset;

my soul behind it, the night only mine,

for only your victorious radiance.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the sunlit offering, sea, August ripeness, and solitary dusk of the speaker.
